name: CA-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 19 points on the partisan baseline
Garamendi is a well-funded incumbent with $1.2M on hand
Republican challenger has raised only ~$20K with $235 cash
Prediction markets price Democratic win at 96%
model.rationale: The district's 19-point Democratic lean, Garamendi's incumbency and large financial advantage, and the challenger's negligible fundraising all point to a comfortable Democratic hold, and markets agree at 96%. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict the fundamentals, the race stays at a roughly 24-point Democratic margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing an unusually weak incumbent margin, or significant outside spending against Garamendi, would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 8th District sits firmly in Democratic territory, with a partisan lean of about 19 points toward Democrats. Longtime incumbent John Garamendi is seeking another term and advanced to the general election. He has raised roughly $489,000 and holds about $1.2 million in cash, giving him a substantial resource advantage.

Republican Rudy Recile has raised only about $20,000 and reported just $235 on hand, with no outside spending on either side. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets price a Democratic win at 96 percent. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and the fundraising gap makes this a Safe Democratic seat.
